en/9-reference/02-messages.title: 9.2 – Messages
en/9-reference/02-messages.content:
Every message starts with [layout-box] and appears once per cause, not once per page. That is
deliberate: with 300 pages and one missing file, 300 identical lines would be no help.
Refusing to read "…" outside of "…"
The path in file leads out of dir. The box outputs nothing.
Usually one .. too many, or a dir that is not what you thought it was. See
2.2.
Snippet file not found: /full/path/to/file
There is no file at that place. The message names the full path — comparing it with where the
file actually is, is the fastest way to the cause.
Under --serve a dashed box appears on the page as well. In a normal build the spot stays empty.
Could not read snippet file (…)
The file is there but could not be read — permissions, a directory instead of a file, a broken
symlink. What the operating system reported is in the brackets. Otherwise it behaves like the
previous one: nothing in a normal build, a box under --serve.
`collapsible` requires a `title`; rendering non-collapsible
collapsible: true without a title. The box is rendered normally, only not collapsible. If the
cause sits in a byLang entry, the message names it.
It is produced while the instance is built, so it only ever sees the configuration. When
collapsible comes from a page’s frontmatter, the console stays silent and the box is quietly
rendered non-collapsible.
No message, no box
There are two causes for that, and neither is a fault:

The snippet is empty. A box without content outputs nothing — deliberately, see
6.2.
The page has hidden the box in its frontmatter.

When nothing at all happens
If the box is absent and the console is silent too, usually the entry itself is not in effect:
enabled: false, or the plugin is installed but not entered in quartz.config.yaml.
When the box sits somewhere else
An entry without a layout block still creates an instance. Quartz places any component that
names no position at its manifest’s default — for this plugin left, with priority: 15
(3.2). Removing the layout block to switch a box off therefore
puts it in the left column; enabled: false is what switches it off.

en/9-reference/03-limits.title: 9.3 – Limits
en/9-reference/03-limits.content:
It filters nothing
A snippet is inserted as it stands — as HTML, unchecked. That is the point: anyone wanting to insert
an <svg> or a <style> should be able to.
The consequence: only use files you control yourself. A snippet from a foreign source is as
trustworthy as foreign JavaScript. That does not apply to values from the page — placeholders are
escaped (4.1).
It knows no conditions
No expressions, no comparisons, no rules per folder. A page can hide a box or swap its snippet,
nothing more. Why, and what helps instead: 6.2.
It renders no Obsidian syntax
Wikilinks, callouts and embeds stay in a Markdown snippet as written. The plugin is a pure component
and sits behind the content pipeline
(1.3).
It remembers nothing in the browser
An opened box is back to whatever collapsed says after the next page change. Without JavaScript it
cannot be otherwise — and shipping no JavaScript is a decision, not a gap
(5.1).
The cache hangs on the modification time
Not on the content. Writing a file back with its old timestamp shows the old version. In practice
this only affects restoring from an archive.
Snippets are public
They live under quartz/static/ and are shipped along. They can be fetched through the site’s
address. For markup that appears on every page anyway that is of no consequence — as a place for
anything non-public the folder is unsuitable.
What is deliberately absent

No scheduling. No box that appears on Monday and disappears on Friday.
No template language. Placeholders insert values; they cannot calculate, branch or repeat.
No built-in styling. Apart from two rules for images the plugin brings no appearance with it
(5.2).

en/index.title: Layout Box
en/index.content:
quartz-layout-box puts a piece of HTML or Markdown anywhere in the Quartz layout: into a
sidebar, the header, the footer, before or after the page body. A word mark, a subtitle, a notice, a
call to action, a line stating where the page stands — anything meant to look the same across many
pages without being written into a theme.
The plugin works entirely at build time and ships no JavaScript to the browser.


                  
                  This site is its own evidence 
                  
                

It is built with the plugin. The word mark at the top left, the chapter name beside it and the box
at the bottom of the left column are three layout boxes; chapter 8 takes
each of them apart.


The nine chapters













































ChapterThe question it answers1 – Getting startedWhat is the plugin for, and how does the first box appear?2 – The snippetFile or configuration, HTML or Markdown?3 – PlacementWhere may a box sit, and in what order?4 – PlaceholdersHow does the page title get into the box?5 – FormHeading, collapsing, your own class — and how to style it6 – Per pageHow does a single page hide or swap the box?7 – Two languagesHow does each language get its own text?8 – RecipesFinished examples, all visible on this page9 – ReferenceEvery option, every message, the glossary
In one minute
npx quartz plugin add github:boxi-os/quartz-layout-box
Create a snippet at quartz/static/snippets/snippet.html, add the entry to quartz.config.yaml,
done:
plugins:
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-layout-box
    enabled: true
    options:
      file: snippet.html
    layout:
      position: left
      priority: 15
At length under 1.2 – Your first box.
Where else it is written
The short version is the repository README — the
same options, without examples. The plugin belongs to
QuartzControl, where it can be set up without writing
YAML; the app is not required, though.

quartz-layout-box setzt ein Stück HTML oder Markdown an eine beliebige Stelle des

Eine Wortmarke, ein Untertitel, ein Hinweis, ein Aufruf, eine Zeile mit dem Stand der Seite — alles,
was auf vielen Seiten gleich aussehen soll, ohne dass man es in ein Theme schreibt.
Das Plugin arbeitet vollständig beim Bauen und liefert kein JavaScript an den Browser aus.


                  
                  Diese Website ist ihr eigener Beleg 
                  
                

Sie ist mit dem Plugin gebaut. Die Wortmarke oben links, der Kapitelname daneben und der Kasten
unten in der linken Spalte sind drei Layout-Boxen; Kapitel 8 nimmt jede davon
auseinander.
